ATP and phosphocreatine are part of the phosphagen system (ATP-PCr system), which provides immediate energy for short-duration, high-intensity activities.  
ATP stores can sustain maximal exertion for only about 1–3 seconds, and phosphocreatine can replenish ATP for an additional 5–8 seconds of intense effort.  
Combined, the total duration is generally accepted in exercise physiology as approximately **5–10 seconds** for maximal exertion before glycolysis becomes the dominant energy source.
